source.title: The Geometry of Harmfulness in LLMs through Subconcept Probing
source.authors: Mcnair Shah; Saleena Angeline; Adhitya Rajendra Kumar; Naitik Chheda; Kevin Zhu; Vasu Sharma; Sean O'Brien; Will Cai

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures the geometry of harmfulness probe directions in LLMs, but does not test superposition, capacity competition/polysemanticity, SAE units, or whether underlying superposed features are one-dimensional. Its related geometry findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.gate_note: The paper trains harmfulness-subconcept probes and measures the rank of their weight-vector subspace, including after ablating each corresponding probe direction from activations. Those results concern related LLM representation geometry but do not test any listed version directly. Jailbreak safety and utility outcomes from steering and ablation are not rows because they do not measure a listed representation claim.
record.test_reason: The paper trains linear probes for 55 harmfulness subcategories in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen-2-7B-Instruct. It measures the effective rank of the probe-weight subspace and steers or ablates along its dominant direction. It cites Toy Models of Superposition only as a source for the linear representation hypothesis. It does not study superposition, sparse features exceeding dimensions, polysemantic neurons, capacity competition or SAE dictionaries. Whether harmfulness concepts use one or several directions is a related question about concept geometry, not about whether superposed features are 1-D, so it goes under fits_no_version. 'cites_only' fits better than 'discusses': superposition is never discussed.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that the 55 subconcept probe directions form a low-rank harmfulness subspace with a single dominant vector. Probes retrained after ablating each direction keep high accuracy, which they read as possible further nonlinear separability. Dominant-direction steering nearly eliminates JailbreakBench harm in Llama with little MMLU loss; in Qwen it reduces but does not eliminate harm. Subspace ablation gives only minor gains.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses linear probes, SVD of probe weights, and activation interventions in LLMs; it does not reproduce the toy-network method in Toy Models of Superposition.
record.method_sensitivity: The effective rank depends on energy threshold and whether probes are trained on base or orthogonalized activations; for Qwen, the reported rank transition occurs at lower energy values and varies more across layers than for Llama. Probe performance also varies by model layer and activation stream.

fits_no_version.finding: Probe directions for 55 harmfulness subcategories have effective rank 1 at τ=0.95 in almost all Llama layers (low-rank, dominant direction). Probes retrained after ablating each subcategory's direction still reach accuracy of at least 0.83 (Llama) and 0.84 (Qwen). The authors suggest each subcategory may be further separable into a nonlinear representation space.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmfulness concepts in instruction-tuned LLMs are dominated by one shared linear direction, but remain linearly decodable after that direction is removed, implying multi-directional concept representations.

record.problems: Only Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen-2-7B-Instruct are tested. The authors note that their tested harmfulness subcategories are limited by the dataset, direction extraction is imprecise, results generalize only to the probed model part, utility tests are limited, and harmfulness evaluation depends on the evaluator model. Some Qwen rank evidence is described through figures without exact thresholds.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows omitted. Steering, ablation, AutoDAN, MMLU, and jailbreak-evaluation outcomes are omitted because they report intervention effects on safety or utility, not on any listed representation claim.

untested.parts: No toy models, no sparsity sweep, no feature-overlap geometry or phase transition.
No neuron-level polysemanticity and no capacity or importance analysis.
No analysis of the causes of polysemantic neurons.
No measure of features spread across neurons and no SAE or dictionary recovery; only supervised linear probes.
Measures the dimensionality of a supervised harmfulness-probe subspace, not whether superposed model features are 1-D or multi-dimensional.

record.verdict_notes: Appendix C also reports that K-means clusters of the probe vectors do not match the dataset's categories (mean adjusted Rand index about 3e-4); this bears on no version. The text inconsistently names the second model 'Qwen-2-7B' and 'Qwen-2.7-7B'. Rows r1–r6 correctly carry versions ['none'].

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature sparsity, overlap geometry, and sparsity-dependent transitions are not tested.
Capacity competition, polysemantic neurons, and importance-dependent dedicated versus shared dimensions are not tested.
The paper does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
It does not measure feature distribution across neurons or recover sparse features with an SAE.
No SAE dictionary features are studied.

The low-rank geometry of harmfulness probe vectors is measured, but the study does not establish whether the model's underlying represented features are one-dimensional or multidimensional, nor whether they are superposed.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Computed effective rank of the harmfulness-subconcept probe weight vectors using SVD.
rows.measure: Effective rank K of harmfulness probe-vector subspace
rows.value: K = 1 for all but the second-to-last layer
rows.note: The paper describes this as low-rank linearity of the harmfulness probe subspace.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for superposition; the reported effective rank measures harmfulness probe geometry, with versions=none.
source_check.problem: Observed low rank does not establish any linked superposition claim.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Computed effective rank of probe vectors trained on activations after ablating each corresponding original probe direction.

conditions.value: classifiers trained on orthogonalized hidden states

rows.measure: Effective rank K of harmfulness probe-vector subspace
rows.baseline: base classifiers reach K = 1 in all but the second-to-last layer at τ = 0.95
rows.value: No layer reaches K = 1 at τ = 0.95; all layers reach K = 1 by τ = 0.84
rows.note: The paper says the orthogonalized-probe subspace is less linear than the base-probe subspace.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for superposition; weaker rank concentration after orthogonalization is not partial evidence for an unlinked claim version.
source_check.problem: The partial state describes probe geometry rather than a tested superposition version.

rows.subject: Qwen-2-7B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Computed effective rank of the harmfulness-subconcept probe weight vectors using SVD.
rows.measure: Effective rank K of harmfulness probe-vector subspace
rows.value: Effective rank quickly drops to one with decreasing energy
rows.note: The text describes the subspace as highly low-rank linear but does not give an exact threshold for this result.
rows.check: For Qwen base probes, Fig. 22a says effective rank quickly drops to one, described as highly low-rank linear. This matches the Llama base result, so 'observed' fits better than 'partial'. The exact energy threshold is not stated.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for superposition; the qualitative rank result is explicitly stated in the Figure 22a caption.
source_check.problem: Low-rank harmfulness probes do not establish any linked superposition claim.

rows.subject: Qwen-2-7B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Computed effective rank of probe vectors trained on orthogonalized hidden states.

conditions.value: lower than for base classifiers; exact value not stated

rows.measure: Effective rank K of harmfulness probe-vector subspace
rows.baseline: base classifiers reach K = 1 at higher energy values
rows.value: Rank drops to one at lower energy values, with more variance between layers than Llama
rows.note: The appendix describes the orthogonalized results as strikingly similar to the base-classifier rank results, but at lower energy and with greater layer variation.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for superposition; the lower energy threshold and layer variation describe probe geometry only.
source_check.problem: The partial state is not grounded in a linked claim version.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Trained new subconcept probes on activations after ablating the corresponding original probe direction.

conditions.value: hidden states orthogonalized against corresponding original probe direction

rows.measure: Held-out test accuracy of orthogonalized-hidden-state probes
rows.value: All values are over 0.83, with a mean of about 0.87
rows.note: The authors interpret these high-accuracy probes as indicating that each subcategory may be further separable into a nonlinear representation space.
rows.check: Locator: Section 2.3 refers to 'Figure 8a' for the full orthogonalized results, but the values (over 0.83, mean about 0.87) come from the Figure 8b caption. Keep Figure 8b.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for superposition; high accuracy after corresponding-direction ablation measures remaining decodability.
source_check.problem: Remaining probe accuracy does not demonstrate feature sharing, distributed neuronal encoding, or SAE recovery.

relation.reason: Elhage et al. (2022) appears as a citation for the linear representation hypothesis; superposition itself is not investigated.

tranche.reason: The paper studies harmfulness probe geometry and interventions; it neither tests nor uses the catalog's superposition claim versions.

source_check.notes: The numerical summaries match the cited prose and captions. States are assessed relative to the catalog's claim versions; versions=none prevents treating these related measurements as observed or partial superposition.
